bible_refs.note: πόρναι μετανοήσαντες ... δικαιοῦνται Ἰωάννῃ πεισθέντες parallels Jesus' saying that tax collectors and prostitutes enter the kingdom before the religious leaders

choices.why: Aorist active participle agreeing with πόρναι, indicating completed action prior to justification
Adverb modifying ῥήμασιν, emphasizing the emptiness of the Pharisees' words

pass_a_gloss: Prostitutes having repented and having done the things pleasing to God are justified by John having been persuaded, even if at first they disobeyed the law, but rather to God; but those saying they keep the law, Pharisees, in mere words only, are rejected by God.
pass_b_english: Prostitutes who have repented and done what is pleasing to God are justified by John, having been persuaded by him, even though at first they disobeyed the law, but rather obeyed God.
But those who claim to keep the law, the Pharisees, in mere words only, are rejected by God.
source_text:
πόρναι μετανοήσαντες καὶ τὰ ἀρεστὰ τῷ θεῷ ποιήσαντες δικαιοῦνται Ἰωάννῃ
πεισθέντες, εἰ καὶ κατ' ἀρχὰς ἠπείθουν τῷ νόμῳ, μᾶλλον δὲ τῷ θεῷ. οἱ δὲ λέγοντες
τηρεῖν τὸν νόμον Φαρισαῖοι ἐν μόνοις ῥήμασιν ψιλοῖς ἀπόβλητοί εἰσιν παρὰ θεῷ·
